7 Best AI Study Tools for Students in 2026
The market of AI study tools has some rare gems. But finding them requires lots of digging. Here are the 7 best AI study tools you can use for free.
Mehal Rashid

AI has had a significant impact on all aspects of our lives. Out of everything it impacted, studies are probably among the areas where AI tools were adopted the quickest. In fact, the Lumina Foundation-Gallup 2026 State of Higher Education study found that 57% of U.S. college students are using AI in their coursework at least weekly.

But now the AI study tools market has become saturated with all sorts of good and useless tools. It has become an overwhelming task to find tools with the best AI for study purposes.

In this guide, we narrow down your search to only the 7 best AI study tools that have implemented AI in genuinely useful ways. 

Read and choose the best free AI study tools to include in your stack without struggling through trial and error by yourself.

How did we evaluate the best AI tools for students?

The list of best AI tools for students coming ahead was curated by keeping in mind the following factors:

A lot of students are struggling with paywall fatigue, so we made sure we only include tools that offer a free forever plan. 
We also picked tools that either use your own documents as their only source of information or have a proven track record for accuracy in technical subjects.
We made sure to choose tools with as few distractions as possible.
Most of these tools work across all your different devices and don't require reading any manual just to get started.
7 best AI study tools for students (Free)

Here's a quick comparison before we dig into each tool:

			
AI Study Tool	Primary Use	Best For	Key AI Feature
RemNote	Flashcard creation and review	Students preparing for high-stakes exams	Auto-generates flashcards from your notes and schedules them via spaced repetition
NotebookLM	Source-based research	Deep dives into dense papers and books	Answers questions only from materials you upload, with citations
Notion	Academic workflow organization	Managing projects, subjects, and notes in one place	AI database builder that creates and fills tables from natural language prompts
Otter.ai	Lecture recording	Students who struggle to take notes during class	Real-time speech-to-text with automated speaker identification
Wolfram Alpha	STEM problem solving	Math, science, and engineering students	Direct computation engine that solves equations from plain English
Khanmigo by Khan Academy	Foundational learning	Building strong fundamentals across K-12 and early college	Khanmigo AI tutor that asks guiding questions instead of giving answers
Napkin.ai	Visualizing ideas	Creating diagrams and graphics for presentations	Turns plain text into flowcharts, diagrams, tables, and roadmaps
1. RemNote (Best for creating and studying with flashcards)

Flashcards are one of the best ways to memorize study material. It has been scientifically proven many times. But to this day, students find it hard to incorporate flashcards into their studies. And it’s not hard to see why it’s like that. The biggest barrier is the amount of time it takes to create paper flashcards from your notes. 

That’s the problem RemNote addresses. Although RemNote is an all-in-one study system, its most promising feature is that it speeds up digital flashcard creation from your notes.

You can take notes during your class, and then upload them to the RemNote app. RemNote will make flashcards from those notes in real-time. You only have to type your notes in a certain way. 

For instance, to make a question-answer flashcard from an information piece, you use two greater-than signs (>>) in that line. For other types of flashcards, you use different symbols. 

You can read our detailed guide to learn how to create all kinds of flashcards in RemNote.

You can also upload your study materials and let the AI scan them to suggest what parts should become flashcards. RemNote then also makes you practice those flashcards using spaced repetition.

You can try RemNote for free.

Key features
Multiple flashcard types (Questions, multi-line, descriptor, cloze, definition,
image occlusion)
AI can provide further explanation for the cards you struggle with
An exam scheduler that builds a custom study plan for you based on the exam date
You can annotate PDFs. Your highlights become flashcards
Multiple ways to practice flashcards (spaced repetition, in order, etc)
You can track your progress across different subjects via stats and graphs.
Pricing

RemNote offers three pricing tiers:

Free forever
Pro: US$10/month
Pro with AI: US$20/month

RemNote also offers lifetime plans.

Pros
Very fast flashcard creation
Syncs your data across all your different devices
25% discount for students
Works on almost every platform and device
The free plan is actually useful for most students
Cons
Has a steep learning curve since there are a lot of features
2. NotebookLM (Best for deep research)

NotebookLM is a product of Google.

It is best defined as a research assistant that only answers your questions from the materials you have uploaded.

First, you create a notebook for a certain subject or a project. Then you upload your study materials to this notebook.

The tool supports a diverse set of file formats. You can upload PDFs, Word docs, images, audio files, website URLs, YouTube links, plain text, and a lot more. You can see all supported file types in the screenshot below.

Once you have uploaded everything, NotebookLM scans your sources and becomes an expert on them. You can then start asking absolutely anything about the content in those sources. 

If you ask a question and the answer isn't in your files, the AI will usually admit it doesn't know instead of making things up.

Using those sources, you can create mind maps, flashcards, quizzes, and audio/video overviews.

Key features
Summarizes multiple sources at once to find common themes
Create podcast-style audio overviews of your notes
Generates practice quizzes and study guides from your files
Supports a wide range of file types
Built-in slide deck and infographics generator
Can create flashcards
Can add sources to notebooks from the web
Pricing

NotebookLM has a free version that allows creating 100 notebooks with 50 sources per notebook.

You can bypass these limits with the paid plans.

NotebookLM is available through Google AI plans. 

Google AI Plus: $7.99/month (100 sources per notebook)
Google AI Pro: $19.99/month (300 sources per notebook)
Google AI Ultra: $249.99/month (600 sources per notebook)
Pros
Doesn’t hallucinate like AI chatbots
Generous free plan
Supports several file formats
Responses always include citations 
Generates different types of media
Cons
Media generation is very slow
Can't answer questions beyond what you've uploaded
3. Notion (Best for organizing projects)

Most students know Notion as a basic place to keep their class notes. But the platform does a lot more than that.

It can manage your entire academic life. You can take notes in it and store them in separate subject-specific folders and subfolders. Notion also allows students to test themselves on their study material. There’s a toggle that hides the answers to questions and makes you actively recall the answer.

You can even set up automated formulas that calculate when you should review a certain topic again based on the spaced repetition method.

Lately, Notion has added AI as well. Now you can just ask AI to build a complex database for you using a natural language prompt instead of manually doing it. The AI is also capable of filling in the blanks in your database from the files in your workspace.

Key features
AI database builder
Automatically extract data and fill in notes
Customizable study trackers for your entire semester
Includes active recall tools
Supports collaboration with classmates on group projects
Integrated portfolio builder
Pricing

Notion has the following plans and pricing:

Forever free
Plus: $12/member/month
Business: $24/member/month
Enterprise: custom price
Pros
Replaces several different apps
Highly customizable
Can organize massive amounts of information
Syncs your data across your phone, tablet, and computer
Can help build long-term memory
Cons
The mobile app can be a bit laggy
Steep learning curve because there are so many different options to explore
4. Otter.ai (Best for lecture recording)

 

Taking notes while a professor is talking isn’t everyone’s cup of tea. Most of us usually end up missing half of what was said because we were too busy writing down a definition from two minutes ago.

Otter.ai solves that problem by doing the note-taking on your behalf. With the app on your phone, you audio-record the lecture with it, and the app turns whatever it hears into a text transcript in real time.

The coolest part is that it can tell different speakers apart. Imagine the potential of this in a small group discussion or a seminar where several people are talking.

Otter.ai also integrates with apps like Zoom or Google Meet to support lecture recording during online classes. It can even listen for specific things, like when your teacher assigns a due date or mentions a surprise quiz, and then turns those into action items for you.

Key features
Speech to text in real-time
Automated speaker identification
Integration with platforms like Zoom and Microsoft Teams
Identifies the main topic of the lecture from keywords
AI-generated summaries
Auto-generates action items
Searchable transcripts
Pricing

Otter.ai offers the following plans and pricing:

Free forever
Pro: $16.99/user/month
Business: $24/user/month
Enterprise: custom
Pros
Reduces the stress of taking notes in class
Extremely helpful for students with hearing or language barriers
Syncs with your calendar to automatically join and record meetings
Cons
Transcriptions can sometimes be inaccurate
Struggles with heavy accents
Currently only supports transcription for the English language
The free version has strict limits
5. Wolfram Alpha (Best for STEM subjects)

Wolfram Alpha is a computational knowledge engine with its own massive database of curated information.

The tool is best for studying math and other science subjects, mainly. But the fields of society and culture are also supported. 

You can ask questions in plain English about any subject without caring about including the right symbols. 

For example, you can just describe a complex integral in words, and Wolfram will calculate its integral instantly. Apart from the answer, you’re also shown the steps leading up to the answer. 

The tool can even generate high-quality graphs.

Key features
Translates plain English into math
Shows the logic behind every answer
Offers graphing tools
Advanced computation for complex calculus and differential equations
Massive database covering science, engineering, finance, etc
Pricing

Wolfram Alpha has the following plans:  

Basic free forever
Pro: $9.99/month
Pro Premium: $12/month
Pros
Extremely high accuracy for math and science problems
Very easy to use
Helps you learn the process of a problem
Reliable for factual data because it uses curated sources
Cons
Struggles with niche topics
Step-by-step solutions are locked behind the paid subscription
6. Khan Academy’s Khanmigo (Best for foundational learning)

We all have used Khan Academy at least once in our lives for one thing or another. 

It is well known for being a non-profit that offers completely free lessons on just about every subject you can think of.

In 2023, they added an AI tutor called Khanmigo. You can use this AI tutor as your 24/7 study buddy to work through tough problems. For instance, if you were solving a chemistry equation, Khanmigo would ask you questions to lead you to the right answer.

The AI can even mark your college admission essays.

Key features
Guides you to answers without giving them away
Real-time feedback on creative writing assignments
Practice quizzes
Debate mode
Pricing

Khan Academy is 100% free for students and other independent users. But Khanmigo has paid plans for individuals, families, and districts. 

There are three plans: 

For Individuals: $4/month
For Families: $4/month
For Districts: Custom
Pros
Encourages active learning
Designed specifically for an educational environment
Covers a massive range of subjects
Excellent for building strong fundamentals
Cons
Sometimes makes silly mistakes
Most of the advanced AI features are currently limited to English
Can feel a bit too simple for students doing very high-level university math
7. Napkin.ai (Best for visualizing ideas)

 

Sometimes we have a really great idea in our heads, but we just can't seem to draw it out so others can understand it. Or we can, but it’ll take us too much time. 

You can turn to Napkin.ai to turn your ideas into visuals. 

The tool simply requires you to paste in a paragraph or a few messy notes from a lecture. Based on your content, it instantly generates visuals such as diagrams, flowcharts, tables, roadmaps, and much more. 

The tool has a built-in AI that can generate the text for you based on what you want to create visuals. 

When you are finished, you can download your work as a picture or a PowerPoint slide to use in class.

Key features
Text to visual generation
Built-in AI helps you brainstorm ideas
Export formats include PNG, PDF, SVG, etc
Library of different icons and fonts
Prompts can be written in more than sixty different languages
Drag and drop canvas for making quick edits to your visuals
Pricing

Napkin.ai has the following plans:

Free forever
Plus: $12/person/month
Pro: $30/person/month
Pros
Extremely fast at making graphics from text
Very easy to use
Generous free plan
Makes dense information easier to understand
Cons
AI-generated text can be basic
Design options can feel repetitive after a while
Advanced features like SVG exports are behind a paywall
Only works on desktop browsers at the moment
RemNote: The best AI tool for studying

All the tools we covered are best at what they do. They all form a complete toolkit of the best AI study tools.

One app you cannot miss out on from this list is RemNote. That’s because in studies, everything boils down to memorization at the end of the term. 

So you must have a memorization tool in your toolkit. 

RemNote makes sure you’re learning things for the long run. It makes flashcards from your study materials and makes you study them using the spaced repetition method, so the knowledge stays in your long-term memory.

Go ahead and sign up for RemNote for free today and try it out.
